model.name: Data Schema / Data Contract
model.purpose: Govern the semantics, structural and value constraints, and producer-consumer agreement that an instance, dataset, or stream must satisfy, independently of how the agreement is stored or served.
model.scope_statement: This model covers a format-neutral schema or data contract as a governed agreement: identity and dialect, logical and physical structure, value domains and data-element meaning, constraints and shapes, composition and references, quality rules bound to schema elements, delivery and retention SLAs that the contract promises, consumer access roles, compatibility and evolution, and validation evidence. JSON, YAML, RDF, Avro JSON, OpenAPI documents, Git, MCP and document stores are projections of this model, not its semantics.
in_scope: Identity, naming, namespace, dialect, meta-schema and version of a schema resource or data contract
Logical objects, properties, types, formats, enumerations, cardinality, keys and nested structure
Semantic meaning of data elements, including data-element concepts, value domains, business names, tags and classification
Constraint languages and shape targeting used to assert validity of instances
Producer-consumer agreement terms: intended use, limitations, quality rules, SLA properties, and consumer roles
Schema evolution, compatibility, canonical form, fingerprints, and validation or conformance reports
Alignments to JSON Schema, SHACL, Apache Avro, OpenAPI Schema Object and ISO/IEC 11179 data-specification metadata
out_of_scope: Dataset or record instances themselves, including dataset catalog identity, partitions as data, and observed statistics of a particular load (WM-DAT-001)
Data-product packaging, marketplace pricing, support channels and product SLAs that are not schema-bound (Open Data Product Standard)
API path, operation, parameter and security-scheme definitions; only the Schema Object is aligned
Physical servers, clusters, warehouses and network endpoints as infrastructure assets
Full ontologies, concept systems and knowledge-graph reasoning beyond constraint shapes
Pipeline, job and transformation-runtime models; documented transform logic on a property is in scope only as contract documentation
Legal privacy-policy documents, DPIAs and consent records as standalone artefacts
Vendor internals of quality engines (Soda, Great Expectations, dbt, Monte Carlo) except as referenced custom rule payloads

boundary_notes.distinction: A dataset holds instance data and claims conformance to one or more schemas or contracts. This model is the agreement and type structure, not the data. Do not duplicate dataset identity, physical location of files, or observed row counts of a load here except as contract quality or SLA terms.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Open Data Product Standard / data product
boundary_notes.distinction: ODCS deprecated the dataProduct field in v3.1.0. Product packaging, ownership of a product portfolio and commercial terms belong to a data-product sibling. This model may name a domain or tenant and bind schema to a product only by reference.

OpenAPI paths, operations, servers and security schemes describe an API surface. The Schema Object is a superset of JSON Schema 2020-12 and is the only OpenAPI construct aligned here. Do not model HTTP methods or path templates as schema elements.

ISO/IEC 11179-32 and OWL describe concept systems. This model uses ISO/IEC 11179-31 data-element concepts and SHACL shapes as constraints over instance graphs, not as a substitute for an ontology model. Full RDFS inferencing is optional in SHACL and is not required here.
ODCS physicalType and physicalName map a logical element onto a table, topic or file type. Engine topology, credentials and server inventory are infrastructure, not schema semantics.

sources.title: Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS) v3.1.0
sources.organization: Bitol / LF AI and Data Foundation (Linux Foundation)
sources.relevance: Normative structure of a data contract: fundamentals (id, version, status, domain, purpose, limitations), schema objects and properties, logical and physical types, quality rules, SLA properties including retention and end of life, and consumer roles.

sources.title: JSON Schema: A Media Type for Describing JSON Documents (Core)
sources.relevance: Canonical schema-resource identity ($id, $anchor, $ref), dialect and vocabulary ($schema, $vocabulary), applicators, assertions versus annotations, and evaluation output independent of storage format.

sources.title: JSON Schema Validation: A Vocabulary for Structural Validation of JSON
sources.relevance: Assertion keywords for type, enum, const, numeric bounds, string pattern and length, array and object cardinality, required and dependentRequired, format, content encoding, and metadata such as deprecated, readOnly, writeOnly, default and examples.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Node and property shapes, targets, property paths, constraint components (datatype, count, pattern, class, closed), severity, deactivation, and validation reports over RDF data graphs.

sources.title: Apache Avro Specification
sources.relevance: Named types, namespaces, fields, unions, defaults, aliases, schema resolution between writer and reader, Parsing Canonical Form, fingerprints, and logical types (decimal, uuid, date, timestamp, duration).

sources.title: ISO/IEC 11179-31:2023 Information technology — Metadata registries (MDR) — Part 31: Metamodel for data specification registration
sources.relevance: Registration of data elements, data-element concepts, object classes, properties, conceptual domains, value meanings, value domains, datatypes and permissible values, independent of bits-and-bytes physical representation.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification v3.1.1
sources.relevance: Schema Object as a superset of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, jsonSchemaDialect, OAS base vocabulary, and the boundary that OAS document text is authoritative if a companion JSON Schema differs.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 11179-3:2023 Information technology — Metadata registries (MDR) — Part 3: Metamodel for registry common facilities
sources.relevance: Registry-item identification, designation, definition, registration, classification and mapping facilities that any registered schema or data-element item must carry.

sources.title: Data Contracts: The Complete Guide (ODCS as industry standard; Data Contract Specification deprecated)
sources.version_or_date: accessed 2026-08-25; states ODCS 3.1 as common standard
sources.relevance: Records the competing Data Contract Specification being deprecated in favour of ODCS 3.1, confirming a single open contract standard and the producer-consumer API-for-data framing.

bundles.name: Identity, dialect and governance
bundles.description: How a schema resource or data contract is identified, which language dialect it uses, how it is versioned and classified in a lifecycle, and who has authority to change it.
bundles.rationale: JSON Schema identifies resources by URI; ODCS identifies contracts by UUID plus version and status; ISO/IEC 11179 identifies registered items independently of representation. Agents cannot operate a contract without resolving identity, dialect and stewardship first.

layers.name: Identifiers, names and dialect
layers.description: Master identifiers, global IRIs, local names, namespaces and the meta-schema or standard version that interprets keywords.

findings.name: Contract and schema identity
findings.description: A data contract has a unique id (typically a UUID) plus an optional name; a JSON Schema resource has a canonical URI in $id and optional plain-name $anchor fragments; Avro named types have a case-sensitive fullname of namespace plus name. These are identifiers of the agreement, not of instance data.

questions.text: What authoritative master-system identifier does the governing catalog, schema registry or contract registry assign to this schema or contract?
What governed global identifier or IRI canonically identifies the schema resource, shape or named type regardless of file path?
What human-readable name, namespace and aliases distinguish this contract or named type from others in the same domain?
If no master-system identifier exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and is a calendar date being misused as identity?
answer_data: confirmation that dates are not used as identifiers

data_elements.name: Master-system identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the authoritative catalog, schema registry or contract registry.

data_elements.name: Contract identifier
data_elements.description: ODCS required unique identifier used to reduce name collisions, such as a UUID.

data_elements.name: Schema canonical URI
data_elements.description: JSON Schema $id absolute URI without a non-empty fragment, also used as base URI for relative references.

data_elements.name: Named type fullname
data_elements.description: Avro record, enum or fixed fullname composed of namespace and name; equality is case-sensitive on the fullname.

data_elements.name: Display name
data_elements.description: Optional contract name or schema title used for humans, not as a durable key.

artifacts.name: Identity registration record
artifacts.description: Registry or catalog record binding master-system identifier, canonical URI, name, namespace and aliases for one schema or contract.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Prefer the governing registry key; fall back to canonical URI or IRI; otherwise a Dimension UUID or ULID. Never use a date as the identifier.

findings.name: Dialect, vocabulary and kind
findings.description: The language that interprets the schema must be explicit: ODCS apiVersion and kind DataContract; JSON Schema $schema meta-schema URI and $vocabulary set; OpenAPI jsonSchemaDialect or OAS dialect id; SHACL Core versus SHACL-SPARQL. Companion JSON Schemas for ODCS and OAS are non-authoritative if they conflict with the standard text.

questions.text: Is this artefact a DataContract, a JSON Schema document, a SHACL shapes graph, an Avro schema, or an OpenAPI Schema Object, and which kind value is declared?
Which meta-schema, apiVersion or dialect URI must a processor load before interpreting keywords?
Which vocabularies are required versus optional, and must a processor refuse the schema if an unknown required vocabulary is declared?
If a companion JSON Schema disagrees with the ODCS or OpenAPI standard text, which source is authoritative?

data_elements.name: Kind
data_elements.description: ODCS required kind; valid value is DataContract. Other families use media type or language name instead of this field.

data_elements.name: Standard version
data_elements.description: ODCS apiVersion of the contract standard used to author the document.

data_elements.name: Schema dialect URI
data_elements.description: JSON Schema $schema or OpenAPI jsonSchemaDialect identifying the meta-schema that the document must validate against.

data_elements.name: Vocabularies in use
data_elements.description: Map of vocabulary URIs to required-or-optional booleans from $vocabulary.

data_elements.name: SHACL profile
data_elements.description: Whether processors must implement SHACL Core only or also SHACL-SPARQL constraint components.

artifacts.name: Declared meta-schema or dialect document
artifacts.description: The meta-schema, ODCS version definition or OAS dialect identified by the contract, used to validate the schema itself.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by the dialect or meta-schema URI, not by local filename.

layers.name: Lifecycle, purpose and authority
layers.description: Status, version of the contract itself, intended use, limitations, stewardship and links to authoritative definitions.

findings.name: Version, status and lifecycle
findings.description: ODCS requires a contract version and a status such as proposed, draft, active, deprecated or retired, and SLA properties may add generalAvailability, endOfSupport and endOfLife. JSON Schema deprecated marks a property or whole resource as to be avoided. SHACL sh:deactivated makes a shape always conform. These are lifecycle states of the agreement, not of instance rows.

questions.text: What is the current version of this data contract or schema, and how does it differ from the language standard version?
What is the current lifecycle status, and which transitions to deprecated, retired, deactivated or end of life are authorised?
Is deprecation or deactivation scoped to the whole contract, a shape, or a single property, and what replacement should consumers use?
When did this contract become generally available, and when are end of support and end of life scheduled?

data_elements.name: Contract version
data_elements.description: ODCS required current version of the data contract, distinct from apiVersion.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle status
data_elements.description: Current status; ODCS examples are proposed, draft, active, deprecated, retired.

data_elements.name: Deprecated flag
data_elements.description: JSON Schema boolean indicating applications should refrain from using the property or resource.

data_elements.name: Shape deactivated
data_elements.description: SHACL sh:deactivated; a true value means all nodes conform to the shape.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle event times
data_elements.description: SLA generalAvailability, endOfSupport and endOfLife values as event times.

artifacts.name: Version and status history
artifacts.description: Serial record of contract versions, status transitions and scheduled GA, end-of-support and end-of-life events.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify each revision by master-system version id plus contract id; timestamps are event metadata, not identifiers.

findings.name: Purpose, stewardship and authoritative definitions
findings.description: ODCS description.purpose, limitations and usage state why the data exists and what is forbidden. Tenant and domain locate stewardship. Authoritative definitions link to catalog, licence, privacy statement or implementation. ISO/IEC 11179 requires designation, definition and registration of the item.

questions.text: What intended purpose, recommended usage and explicit limitations apply to consumers of this contract?
Which tenant, domain, data product owner or data steward is accountable for this contract?
Which authoritative definition URLs supply business meaning, licence, privacy terms or implementation mapping?
Who authored or registered this definition, and when was the definition event versus when was it ingested?

data_elements.name: Purpose
data_elements.description: Intended purpose for the provided data.

data_elements.name: Limitations
data_elements.description: Technical, compliance and legal limitations for data use.

data_elements.name: Tenant and domain
data_elements.description: Property the data is associated with and the logical data domain name.

data_elements.name: Authoritative definitions
data_elements.description: List of links with type such as businessDefinition, implementation or transformationImplementation.

data_elements.name: Registrar
data_elements.description: Party that registered the metadata item under ISO/IEC 11179 registration facilities.

artifacts.name: Authoritative definition set
artifacts.description: Collected links and texts that constitute the business definition, licence, privacy notice or implementation mapping for the contract or element.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify each definition by its URL plus type; do not treat the retrieved page title as the contract identifier.

bundles.name: Semantic and structural model
bundles.description: Objects, properties, logical and physical types, value domains and the conceptual meaning of data elements.
bundles.rationale: ODCS separates objects and properties and ties business names to physical types. JSON Schema and Avro define instance data models. ISO/IEC 11179-31 separates a data-element concept from its value domain so meaning is not collapsed into a storage type.

layers.name: Objects, properties and types
layers.description: Structural elements and the logical versus physical type system.

findings.name: Objects, properties and nesting
findings.description: ODCS v3 schema is a list of elements: objects (table, document, topic, file) contain properties (columns, fields). Arrays use items. JSON Schema models object, array, primitives and null. Avro adds record, enum, map, union and fixed. PhysicalName and physicalType project the logical element onto a store without making the store the schema.

questions.text: Which objects does this schema define, and what is each object's logical type, physical type and physical name?
Which properties belong to each object, in what order, and which nested object or array items do they contain?
What is the declared data granularity of each object, such as grain of aggregation or uniqueness of a row?
Which refactor-safe element identifiers should be used in references instead of names that may change?

data_elements.name: Schema element list
data_elements.description: ODCS required schema array of objects and properties to be catalogued.

data_elements.name: Element identifier
data_elements.description: Optional stable id for refactor-safe references to an object or property.

data_elements.name: Element name
data_elements.description: Required name of the object or property in the schema.

data_elements.name: Physical projection
data_elements.description: physicalName and physicalType such as table, view, topic, file or VARCHAR(18).

data_elements.name: Array items
data_elements.description: Item schema when logicalType is array, including nested objects.

artifacts.name: Structural schema definition
artifacts.description: The object and property tree of the contract, independent of YAML or JSON serialisation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify the structure by contract or schema resource id plus element ids; names are labels.

findings.name: Types, formats and value domains
findings.description: JSON Schema instance types are null, boolean, object, array, number and string, with integer as a numeric subtype. ODCS logicalType is string, date, timestamp, time, number, integer, object, array or boolean, refined by logicalTypeOptions (pattern, min/max, format, timezone). Avro primitives and logical types encode date and timestamp as ints and longs. ISO/IEC 11179 value domains and permissible values supply representation without implying meaning. JSON Schema format is annotation by default and assertion only when the format-assertion vocabulary is required.

questions.text: What logical type, format, pattern and bounds apply to each property, and is format an annotation or an assertion?
How does the logical type map to a physical datatype, Avro primitive or logical type, and are timezone or precision declared?
What enumerated symbols, const values or described permissible values constitute the value domain?
If the property represents time or location, which calendar, offset, geometry encoding or coordinate reference is required?

data_elements.name: Logical type
data_elements.description: ODCS logicalType or JSON Schema type / Avro type name.

data_elements.name: Logical type options
data_elements.description: Bounds, pattern, format, timezone and collection options that refine the logical type.

data_elements.name: Format attribute
data_elements.description: JSON Schema format such as date-time, uuid, email, uri, or ODCS string format analogue.

data_elements.name: Value domain
data_elements.description: Enumerated or described set of permissible values, Avro enum symbols, or JSON Schema enum/const.

data_elements.name: Avro logical type
data_elements.description: decimal, uuid, date, time-millis, timestamp-micros and related logical-type attributes.

artifacts.name: Type and value-domain map
artifacts.description: Per-property mapping of logical type, physical type, format, timezone and permissible values.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Key by element id; type names are not identifiers of the property.

layers.name: Concepts, meaning and classification
layers.description: Business names, data-element concepts, tags, sensitivity classification and critical data elements.

findings.name: Data-element concepts and classification
findings.description: ISO/IEC 11179-31 registers a data element as a concept (object class plus property) plus a value domain. ODCS businessName, description, tags, classification (for example public or restricted), criticalDataElement and encryptedName capture business meaning and sensitivity without being a privacy-policy model. Tags may appear at any element level.

questions.text: What business name, data-element concept, object class and property meaning does this element represent independently of its datatype?
What classification, tags and critical-data-element flag apply, and which code list authorises those values?
If values are encrypted at rest or in motion, what is the encrypted element name and how does it relate to the plaintext property?
Does this element carry personal or otherwise restricted data such that access, masking or purpose limitation in the contract must be enforced?

data_elements.name: Business name
data_elements.description: Business name of the element, distinct from physical or technical name.

data_elements.name: Data element concept
data_elements.description: ISO/IEC 11179 concept that can be represented as a data element, described independently of representation.

data_elements.name: Classification
data_elements.description: Sensitivity or handling classification such as public, restricted or confidential.

data_elements.name: Tags
data_elements.description: Categorisation tags that may appear at contract or element level, for example finance or employee_record.

data_elements.name: Critical data element flag
data_elements.description: Boolean indicating whether the element is a critical data element.

data_elements.name: Encrypted name
data_elements.description: Name of the element that holds the encrypted value corresponding to this property.

artifacts.name: Concept and classification record
artifacts.description: Business meaning, registered data-element concept, tags and sensitivity classification for an element.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify the concept by administered registry item id or IRI; classification codes are not element identifiers.

bundles.name: Constraints, shapes and composition
bundles.description: Assertions that instances must satisfy, how subschemas and shapes are applied, and how reusable fragments are referenced.
bundles.rationale: JSON Schema is a constraint system whose keywords assert or apply subschemas. SHACL groups constraints into targeted shapes. Avro encodes presence via types, unions and defaults rather than independent assertions. Agents must not treat these semantics as interchangeable without an explicit mapping.

layers.name: Assertions, cardinality and keys
layers.description: Type checks, bounds, patterns, required fields, uniqueness and primary keys.

findings.name: Structural and value constraints
findings.description: JSON Schema asserts type, enum, const, multipleOf, min/max, length, pattern, min/maxItems, uniqueItems, required, dependentRequired and object property counts. Missing keywords must not fail. Keywords targeting another primitive type pass automatically. ODCS required, unique, primaryKey and primaryKeyPosition, plus logicalTypeOptions, express the same surface for tabular contracts. SHACL adds minCount, maxCount, datatype, pattern, class, nodeKind and closed shapes with ignored properties.

questions.text: Which properties are required or unique, what are min and max counts, and is the shape closed against extra properties?
Which numeric bounds, string patterns, enums and formats must instance values satisfy?
Which properties form a primary or compound key, and in what position?
Which constraints are warnings rather than violations, and which exceptions or ignored properties are authorised?

data_elements.name: Required
data_elements.description: Whether the element may contain null or be absent; ODCS default is false. JSON Schema required lists property names that must be present.

data_elements.name: Cardinality bounds
data_elements.description: minCount/maxCount, minItems/maxItems, minProperties/maxProperties or ODCS equivalents.

data_elements.name: Pattern and numeric bounds
data_elements.description: pattern, minLength, maxLength, minimum, maximum, exclusive bounds, multipleOf.

data_elements.name: Primary key
data_elements.description: ODCS primaryKey boolean and primaryKeyPosition for compound keys.

data_elements.name: Closed shape
data_elements.description: SHACL sh:closed and sh:ignoredProperties, or JSON Schema additionalProperties/unevaluatedProperties behaviour.

artifacts.name: Constraint set
artifacts.description: The collection of assertions that apply to a schema element or shape, including keys and closed-world rules.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify constraints by parent element or shape IRI plus constraint component; do not use natural-language rule text as identity.

layers.name: Composition, references and shapes
layers.description: Reusable fragments, applicators, property paths and validation targets.

findings.name: Composition, references and shape targets
findings.description: JSON Schema applicators apply subschemas in place or to children via $ref, $defs, allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if/then/else, properties, prefixItems and $dynamicRef. $id in a subschema starts a new resource. SHACL distinguishes node shapes from property shapes with sh:path (predicate, inverse, sequence, alternative, quantified paths) and targets class, node, subjects-of and objects-of. Avro references named types by fullname and uses unions instead of oneOf. OpenAPI Schema Object $ref follows JSON Schema 2020-12 inside schemas.

questions.text: Which reusable definitions exist, and which $ref, named-type or shape IRIs must be resolved before evaluation?
How are subschemas combined (allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, union), and does adding a constraint follow open-world JSON Schema rules or Avro field lists?
Which nodes does each SHACL shape target, and what property path is constrained from the focus node?
What happens if a reference cannot be dereferenced, or if $dynamicRef depends on evaluation-time dynamic scope?

data_elements.name: Schema references
data_elements.description: $ref, $dynamicRef, Avro named-type references or SHACL sh:node links.

data_elements.name: Reusable definitions
data_elements.description: $defs (and legacy definitions) or named Avro types available for reference.

data_elements.name: Applicators
data_elements.description: allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if/then/else or Avro union ordered branches.

data_elements.name: Shape targets
data_elements.description: SHACL targetClass, targetNode, targetSubjectsOf, targetObjectsOf or implicit class targets.

data_elements.name: Property path
data_elements.description: SHACL well-formed property path mapping to a SPARQL path.

artifacts.name: Shapes graph or subschema set
artifacts.description: Reusable shapes, $defs and named types that the root schema applies by reference or applicator.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by canonical URI, shape IRI or Avro fullname of each reusable resource.

bundles.name: Producer-consumer agreement, quality and access
bundles.description: Contract terms beyond structure: quality rules, delivery SLAs including retention, and roles that grant access.
bundles.rationale: ODCS treats a data contract as an enforceable agreement, not only a type tree. Quality, SLA and roles are first-class sections. Dataset-level quality observations still belong with WM-DAT-001; this model stores the promised rules.

layers.name: Quality rules and dimensions
layers.description: Promised data-quality checks bound to schema elements.

findings.name: Quality rules bound to schema
findings.description: ODCS quality entries are text, library metrics (nullValues, missingValues, invalidValues, duplicateValues, rowCount), SQL, or custom engine payloads. Operators such as mustBe and mustBeBetween compare a metric to a threshold. Dimensions include accuracy, completeness, conformity, consistency, coverage, timeliness and uniqueness. Severity, businessImpact and schedule are part of the rule. SHACL severity (Info, Warning, Violation) is the RDF analogue for constraint outcomes.

questions.text: Which quality rules are bound to each object or property, of what type, metric and dimension, and what operator threshold must hold?
In what unit is the metric expressed, and is the comparison in rows, percent or another unit?
When is each quality rule scheduled to run, and what severity and business impact apply on failure?
What evidence artefact proves a quality rule passed or failed for a given evaluation event?

data_elements.name: Quality rule identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier for a quality rule used in references.

data_elements.name: Quality type
data_elements.description: text, library, sql or custom.

data_elements.name: Metric and operator
data_elements.description: Library metric name, arguments, comparison operator and unit.

data_elements.name: Quality dimension
data_elements.description: accuracy, completeness, conformity, consistency, coverage, timeliness or uniqueness.

data_elements.name: SQL or custom implementation
data_elements.description: SQL query with {object}/{property} placeholders, or vendor engine name plus implementation block.

artifacts.name: Quality rule definition
artifacts.description: A promised quality check, including metric or implementation and its schedule. Distinct from an observed dataset score.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by quality.id or a Dimension UUID; engine-specific names are not master identifiers.

layers.name: SLA, availability and retention
layers.description: Service-level properties the producer promises for contracted elements.

findings.name: SLA properties including retention
findings.description: ODCS slaProperties bind a property such as latency, frequency, timeOfAvailability, availability, throughput, errorRate, timeToDetect, timeToNotify, timeToRepair, generalAvailability, endOfSupport, endOfLife or retention to an element path, value, optional unit and driver (regulatory, analytics, operational). Retention is a contract term about how long data remains available, not a storage-engine backup policy.

questions.text: Which SLA properties are promised, on which elements, with what values, units and drivers?
What latency, frequency and time of availability apply, and under which scheduler?
What retention period is contracted, when does deletion or end of life occur, and which regulatory driver requires it?
Which SLA misses are authorised exceptions, and what time-to-detect, notify and repair apply when a miss occurs?

data_elements.name: SLA property identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier for an SLA entry.

data_elements.name: SLA property name
data_elements.description: latency, frequency, retention, availability and related QoS properties.

data_elements.name: SLA value and unit
data_elements.description: Agreement value, optional valueExt and unit using ISO-style units such as d or y.

data_elements.name: SLA element path
data_elements.description: Object.element path the SLA is checked against.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Contracted retention duration or end-of-life timestamp for the element.

artifacts.name: SLA clause
artifacts.description: A contracted service-level clause, including retention and lifecycle dates, bound to schema elements.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by slaProperties.id or contract id plus property and element path.

layers.name: Roles, access and handling
layers.description: Who may consume or produce data under the contract and with what access mode.

findings.name: Consumer roles and access
findings.description: ODCS roles list IAM role names, access mode (read or write), and first- and second-level approvers. JSON Schema readOnly and writeOnly describe instance properties managed exclusively by the owning authority or never returned on read. These are contract-level access terms, not a full IAM model.

questions.text: Which roles may access data under this contract, with what access mode, and who approves grants?
Which properties are readOnly or writeOnly, and what does the owning authority do if a consumer sends or requests them incorrectly?
What is the default access rule when no role matches, and which break-glass exceptions exist?
What decision record authorises a new consumer role binding to this contract?

data_elements.name: Role identifier
data_elements.description: Optional stable id for a role entry.

data_elements.name: Role name
data_elements.description: IAM role name that provides access to the dataset under the contract.

data_elements.name: Access mode
data_elements.description: Type of access provided, for example read or write.

data_elements.name: Approvers
data_elements.description: First- and second-level approvers of the role grant.

data_elements.name: readOnly and writeOnly
data_elements.description: JSON Schema flags for properties managed only by the owning authority or never returned on read.

artifacts.name: Contract role binding
artifacts.description: Declared consumer or producer role, access mode and approval path for this contract.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by role.id or contract id plus role name in the governing IAM or contract registry.

bundles.name: Evolution, validation and interoperability
bundles.description: How schema versions relate, how instances are validated, how canonical form and fingerprints are computed, and how languages align without false conformance claims.
bundles.rationale: Avro defines writer/reader resolution, Parsing Canonical Form and fingerprints. JSON Schema defines evaluation and output. SHACL defines validation reports. Cross-language mapping is alignment, not identity.

layers.name: Compatibility and evolution
layers.description: Rules for changing a schema while remaining usable by existing producers or consumers.

findings.name: Schema resolution and compatibility
findings.description: Avro resolves a writer schema against a reader schema: fields match by name; missing reader fields require defaults; extra writer fields are ignored; numeric and string/bytes promotions are defined; aliases rewrite writer names. Defaults are for reading old data, not for omitting fields at write time. JSON Schema is a constraint system: a new keyword can only add restrictions, never lift one. Enum default on Avro reader handles unknown symbols. These two evolution models conflict if treated as one.

questions.text: What is the writer schema and the reader schema, and do they match under Avro resolution or JSON Schema constraint strengthening?
Which compatibility policy applies (backward, forward, full, or transitive variants), and which field additions or deletions are allowed?
Which reader fields have defaults, which names have aliases, and would a missing default signal an incompatible change?
When a compatibility check fails, what event is recorded and what exception process may override the block?

data_elements.name: Writer schema reference
data_elements.description: Schema used to serialise the data.

data_elements.name: Reader schema reference
data_elements.description: Schema the application expects when deserialising.

data_elements.name: Compatibility policy
data_elements.description: Declared evolution policy. Industry names such as BACKWARD or FULL are alignments to Avro resolution, not Avro specification identifiers.

data_elements.name: Field defaults
data_elements.description: Avro default values used only when reading data that lacks the field.

data_elements.name: Aliases
data_elements.description: Alternate names for types or fields used to map writer names onto reader names.

artifacts.name: Compatibility check report
artifacts.description: Result of comparing two schema versions under the declared resolution or constraint-strengthening rules.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by pair of schema version identifiers plus policy; the check time is event metadata.

layers.name: Validation process and reports
layers.description: How processors evaluate instances and what evidence they emit.

findings.name: Validation and conformance reporting
findings.description: JSON Schema evaluation applies the root schema to the instance, collecting assertion booleans and annotations; recommended output is itself schema-described. An instance is valid when all locations satisfy asserted constraints. SHACL validation takes a data graph and a shapes graph and produces a validation report with sh:conforms and sh:result entries (focus node, path, value, source constraint component, severity, message). Conformance checking is the boolean simplification. Processors may fail closed on ill-formed shapes or unsupported entailment.

questions.text: What instance, schema or shapes graph, dialect and engine are inputs to a validation run?
Did the instance conform, and which results with severity, path and value were produced?
When did the validation event occur, and when was the report ingested, if those times differ?
Which annotations (title, default, format) were collected from successful schemas, and are they used as evidence or only as hints?

data_elements.name: Conforms
data_elements.description: Boolean result of validation or SHACL sh:conforms.

data_elements.name: Validation results
data_elements.description: Per-location failures or SHACL validation results including path, value, component and message.

data_elements.name: Result severity
data_elements.description: SHACL Info, Warning or Violation, or ODCS quality severity.

data_elements.name: Evaluation event time
data_elements.description: When validation ran, distinct from when the report was stored.

artifacts.name: Validation report
artifacts.description: Conformance boolean plus detailed results for one evaluation of an instance against a schema or shapes graph.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by evaluation id; include schema id and instance id as references, not as the report's own identity.

layers.name: Canonical form, fingerprints and alignments
layers.description: Normalised schema text, short substitutes for identity, and honest cross-standard mapping.

findings.name: Canonicalization, fingerprints and language alignments
findings.description: Avro Parsing Canonical Form strips docs and aliases, expands fullnames, orders attributes and removes whitespace so two schemas that serialise identically in PCF are the same for readers. Fingerprints of PCF (SHA-256, MD5, CRC-64-AVRO) tag data and cache codecs; they are not security guarantees. JSON Schema $id is an identifier, not necessarily a network locator. OpenAPI Schema Object is a superset of JSON Schema 2020-12 with an OAS dialect. Alignments must record conflicts: JSON Schema is open-world constraints; Avro is a closed data definition with positional binary encoding.

questions.text: What canonical form is used to decide whether two schemas are the same for reading, and which attributes are stripped?
What fingerprint algorithm and digest identify this canonical schema, and is it used as a cache key rather than as a security signature?
Which external standards is this contract aligned to, and which semantic conflicts are recorded instead of claimed conformance?
If string-encoded content declares contentEncoding or contentMediaType, is automatic decode disabled by default as JSON Schema requires for safety?

data_elements.name: Canonical form
data_elements.description: Normalised schema text such as Avro Parsing Canonical Form.

data_elements.name: Schema fingerprint
data_elements.description: Short digest of the canonical form used as a tag or cache key.

data_elements.name: Alignment set
data_elements.description: Named external standards and the mapping notes, including known conflicts.

data_elements.name: Content encoding and media type
data_elements.description: JSON Schema contentEncoding, contentMediaType and optional contentSchema for string-encoded payloads.

artifacts.name: Canonical schema and fingerprint record
artifacts.description: Canonicalised schema text plus fingerprint and declared alignments, including conflict notes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The fingerprint identifies the canonical bytes; the master-system schema id remains the business identifier.

functions.name: Register or publish schema or contract
functions.description: Create a governed schema or data-contract record with identity, dialect, owner and initial lifecycle status.
effects: status is proposed or draft unless policy allows active

functions.name: Validate instance against schema or shapes
functions.description: Evaluate an instance, data graph or batch against the declared schema, contract constraints and optional quality rules.
preconditions: schema is well-formed for the dialect
effects: validation event is recorded with event time
report artefact is stored with ingestion time if different

functions.name: Check schema compatibility
functions.description: Compare a proposed schema version with one or more accepted versions under Avro resolution or JSON Schema constraint-strengthening rules.
preconditions: both schemas share an identity lineage
effects: publish may be blocked on failure

functions.name: Resolve references and compose subschemas
functions.description: Dereference $ref, named types and shape links, applying applicators to produce the effective schema for a location.
effects: evaluation uses the resolved resource set

functions.name: Canonicalize and fingerprint
functions.description: Normalise a schema to Parsing Canonical Form or an agreed JSON canonicalisation and compute a fingerprint.
preconditions: schema is valid for the language
effects: canonical bytes become the comparison basis

functions.name: Evaluate contracted quality rules
functions.description: Run library, SQL or custom quality rules bound to schema elements and compare metrics to operators.
preconditions: SQL dialect matches the target if type is sql
effects: quality evidence is attached to the evaluation event
severity and business impact are available to alerting

functions.name: Retire, deprecate or deactivate
functions.description: Move a contract, property or shape to deprecated, retired or deactivated without erasing history required by retention.
preconditions: replacement is recorded if required by policy
effects: historical versions remain readable per retention

functions.name: Emit conformance report
functions.description: Assemble identity, dialect, validation results, quality outcomes and compatibility status into a single operator-facing report.
preconditions: at least one validation or quality evaluation exists
effects: report is addressable by evaluation id
audit log records who generated it

composition.purpose: A dataset or stream instance claims conformance to this schema or data contract; this model does not store the instance rows.

composition.target: JSON Schema Core and Validation Draft 2020-12
composition.purpose: Default constraint, identity, applicator and annotation semantics for JSON-compatible instances; not a claim that every contract is a JSON Schema document.
Shape targeting, property paths and validation reports for RDF instance graphs.
Named-type, binary-encoding, schema-resolution, canonical-form and fingerprint semantics for streaming and file serialisation.
Reuse JSON Schema 2020-12 as the type system inside API descriptions without importing paths or operations.
Separate data-element concepts, conceptual domains and value domains from physical representation.

composition.target: Open Data Product Standard / data product
composition.purpose: Optional link from a contract domain to a data product; ODCS deprecated an inline dataProduct field in v3.1.0.

owner_package_requirements: A data product owner or data steward accountable for meaning, constraints and consumer agreement
A dialect or language owner who decides which meta-schema, apiVersion and vocabularies are allowed
A registrar or catalog function that issues the authoritative master-system identifier and records registration provenance
A security or privacy reviewer for classified, encrypted or personal-data elements
dimension.namespace_guidance: Place contracts under a governed namespace that concatenates organisation, domain and contract name, and use JSON Schema $id or Avro namespace as the IRI/fullname form. Local element names live under that resource. Do not use file paths, Git branches or collection names as identity. Prefer NAV.INF.DAT.SCH as the navigation path and vr.wm-dat-004 as the registry id.

canonicalization_rules: For Avro, transform to Parsing Canonical Form before comparing or fingerprinting: expand fullnames, keep only type, name, fields, symbols, items, values and size, order those attributes, unescape strings and strip whitespace and docs.
For JSON Schema, treat $id URI normalisation per RFC 3986 as identity canonicalisation; keyword order is not semantically significant except where applicators define array order.
Do not treat YAML key order, Markdown documentation or companion JSON Schema bugs as semantic differences when the governing standard text is unchanged.
patch_rules: Publish a new version rather than silently rewriting an active contract; ODCS version and JSON Schema resource URI should change when meaning or constraints change.
JSON Schema patches may only add constraints for a given location; lifting a constraint is a breaking change and needs a new identifier or an explicit compatibility exception.
Avro patches that add fields without defaults, remove reader fields that writers still produce, or change union order incompatibly must fail the compatibility function unless policy is NONE.
compatibility_rules: Default recommended policy for binary Avro streams is backward compatibility so new readers can read the last writer schema using defaults and aliases.

JSON Schema and SHACL consumers should treat a tightened constraint as requiring consumer coordination; a loosened constraint is a producer-side breaking change for anyone who relied on the old guarantee.
Do not claim OpenAPI, ODCS and Avro documents are interchangeable because each can be serialised as JSON or YAML.

identity_priority: authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the governing catalog, schema registry or contract registry
governed global identifier or IRI such as JSON Schema $id, SHACL shape IRI, Avro fullname, or ISO/IEC 11179 administered item identifier
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system identifier exists
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps MUST use RFC 3339 with required seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Record event time (when the contract change, validation, quality check, SLA occurrence or registration actually happened) separately from observation or ingestion time (when the Dimension recorded that fact) whenever those differ. A date alone is not an identifier and must not replace a master-system key.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts append a monotonic version or fingerprint to the master identifier, for example {contract-id}/v/{version} or {fullname}#{fingerprint}. Do not embed calendar dates as the version unless the dialect URI itself is an official dated spec identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store a content digest of the canonical form with each published version. Avro fingerprints are collision-resistant cache keys, not authentication. Reject evaluation if the dialect is unknown and required, or if the shapes graph is ill-formed.

policies: No contract may move to active status without a master-system or Dimension identifier, a declared dialect, an owner, and a documented purpose or limitations statement.
Publishing a new version MUST run compatibility checks against the policy in force; failures block publish unless an exception with approver and expiry is recorded.
Quality rules and SLA retention clauses are part of the agreement; deleting a retired version before the contracted retention period is a policy breach.
Classification and encryptedName on elements constrain who may read instance values even when the schema document itself is widely readable.

read: Resolve by master-system identifier, canonical URI or Dimension UUID
List versions and status for a contract lineage
Retrieve effective schema after reference resolution
Read validation and compatibility reports by evaluation id
create: Register a draft contract or schema with kind, dialect, owner and identity
Create first version with status proposed or draft
Attach initial quality, SLA and role clauses
update: Add a new version; do not overwrite an active canonical artefact in place
Change status along the allowed lifecycle
Patch documentation and tags that do not alter constraints without a version bump only when policy allows annotation-only edits
delete: Retire or deactivate rather than hard-delete while retention or legal hold applies
Tombstone a version after retention expires
Never reuse a retired identifier for a different meaning

roles.name: Data product owner or data steward
responsibilities: Accountable for purpose, limitations, business names and consumer agreement
Approves status transitions to active, deprecated or retired

roles.name: Schema author
responsibilities: Authors structure, types, constraints and references
Keeps dialect, $id or fullname and element ids coherent

roles.name: Quality engineer
responsibilities: Defines library, SQL or custom quality rules and schedules

roles.name: Consumer
responsibilities: Binds to a version under an approved role
Reports contract breaches and requests schema changes

roles.name: Registrar
responsibilities: Records designation, definition and registration metadata per ISO/IEC 11179 facilities

roles.name: Security and privacy reviewer
responsibilities: Reviews classification, encryptedName, readOnly/writeOnly and role grants
Authorises exceptions to default deny on sensitive elements

access.default_rule: Schema documents that contain no restricted classifications are readable by authenticated agents in the Dimension; instance-level access follows contract roles and defaults to deny when no role matches.
exceptions: Break-glass read of a restricted contract for incident response, with dual approval and time-boxed grant
Compatibility override that publishes an incompatible version with recorded decision and consumer notice
audit_requirements: Log register, publish, status change, compatibility override, validation run and role grant with actor, event time and target identifier
Retain audit records at least as long as the contract retention SLA

coverage.claim: This structure covers the defensible operating surface of a format-neutral data schema and data contract: identity, dialect, lifecycle, semantic structure, constraints and shapes, quality and SLA agreement, access roles, evolution, validation evidence and major language alignments. It is not a universal theory of all schema languages or of dataset instances.

checklist.notes: ODCS id, JSON Schema $id/$anchor, Avro fullname, ISO/IEC 11179 administered identifiers, and Dimension UUID fallback.
ODCS status and version; deprecated; SHACL deactivated; SLA generalAvailability, endOfSupport, endOfLife.
Dataset conformance, $ref and named-type links, SHACL targets and paths, role bindings, authoritative definition URLs.
Lifecycle and SLA times, quality schedules, validation event versus ingestion time, timestamp formats and timezones.
Registration author, authoritative definitions, transformLogic as documented derivation, writer schema accompanying Avro data.
Steward or product owner, tenant, domain, registrar, readOnly owning authority.
JSON Schema evaluation, SHACL reports, ODCS quality operators, compatibility checks.
ODCS roles and approvers, JSON Schema readOnly/writeOnly, default deny for unmatched roles.
SLA retention and endOfLife as contract terms; retire-versus-hard-delete policy.
Alignments to JSON Schema, SHACL, Avro, OpenAPI Schema Object and ISO/IEC 11179, with recorded conflicts.
Business names, data-element concepts, value domains, tags and classification.
Cardinality, keys, patterns, closed shapes, applicators and quality rules.
No primary-fetched GeoJSON, Simple Features or CRS profile; only a probe question under types.

known_omissions: W3C XML Schema, RELAX NG, Protocol Buffers, Apache Thrift, GraphQL SDL, LinkML, FHIR StructureDefinition, Parquet and Arrow type systems were not fetched as primary sources and are not modelled as canonical.
SHACL 1.2 Core is a Working Draft as of 2026 and is not treated as replacing the 2017 Recommendation.
ODCS team, infrastructure, pricing and support-channel sections were not independently fetched; team rosters and servers remain out of scope or gaps.
ODCS v3.2 and AI-oriented contract features are in progress and lack a frozen primary specification.
Multi-party negotiation, cryptographic signing of contracts, and schema-registry product APIs (for example Confluent subject compatibility names) lack primary support here.
Geometry, CRS and raster schemas are omitted beyond noting the gap.
conflicts: JSON Schema is an open-world constraint system (keywords add restrictions; missing keywords do not fail; type is not implied). Avro is a closed data-definition language with required fields at write time and positional binary encoding. Treating them as the same evolution model is incorrect.
ODCS and OpenAPI companion JSON Schemas are explicitly non-authoritative if they disagree with the standard text.
JSON Schema $id is a URI that need not be dereferenceable; ODCS id is a UUID-like unique key; Avro identity is a fullname. These are alignments, not one identifier system.
JSON Schema format is annotation by default; requiring the format-assertion vocabulary changes interoperability.
The prior Data Contract Specification is deprecated in favour of ODCS 3.1; do not claim dual-standard conformance.
OpenAPI 3.0 nullable versus 3.1 type arrays is a dialect break inside the Schema Object family.
SHACL closed shapes and JSON Schema additionalProperties/unevaluatedProperties implement similar intent with different defaults and path semantics.
regional_assumptions: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 timestamps with explicit offsets are the interchange profile; ODCS examples include named timezones such as Australia/Sydney which must be reduced to offset at the event boundary.
Classification values (public, restricted, confidential) and IAM role names are organisation-specific code lists, not a global taxonomy.
SQL quality rules are dialect-specific to the target engine; no translation service is provided by ODCS.
Retention SLAs may be driven by regional law (for example GDPR storage limitation) but this model records the contracted period, not the legal instrument.
ECMA-262 regular-expression interoperability limits apply to JSON Schema and ODCS pattern fields.
adversarial_checks: Would a date or filename be accepted as the contract identifier? Rejected: identity priority forbids dates as identifiers and prefers master-system keys.
Could an agent claim Avro backward compatibility while publishing a JSON Schema that lifts a constraint? Flagged as a recorded conflict, not allowed as silent equivalence.
Could YAML versus JSON serialisation be treated as a semantic change? Rejected: storage format is a projection.
Could companion JSON Schema bugs override ODCS or OpenAPI text? Rejected: the standard text takes precedence.
Could SHACL 1.2 WD features be required as if they were 2017 Rec? Marked as an omission; processors must declare the Rec profile.
Could quality rowCount of a particular load be stored as schema structure? Rejected: promised rules live here, observed dataset measures live in WM-DAT-001.
